mcqs.question: How does the atomic radius change as we move down a group in the periodic table?

options.D: It first increases and then decreases

mcqs.explanation: When we go down a group, each successive element has an additional electron shell, making the distance from the nucleus to the outermost electrons larger. Hence atomic radius increases steadily. Options A and B are opposite to the observed trend, and D does not describe the systematic behavior.

mcqs.question: Which ion is larger in size?

options.D: It depends on the crystal lattice

mcqs.explanation: When an atom loses an electron to form a cation (Na⁺), its electron cloud contracts, making it smaller than the parent atom. Gaining an electron to form an anion (Cl⁻) adds electron‑electron repulsion, expanding the cloud. Therefore Cl⁻ is larger than Na⁺. Options A and C are incorrect, and D is irrelevant to the intrinsic ionic size.

mcqs.question: What is the definition of atomic radius as used in periodic trends?

options.A: The distance from the nucleus to the outermost electron in an isolated atom
options.B: Half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms of the element when they are in contact
options.C: The radius of the atomic nucleus
options.D: The distance between two bonded atoms in a molecule

mcqs.answer: Half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms of the element when they are in contact
mcqs.explanation: Atomic radius is defined operationally as half the internuclear distance between two identical, unbonded atoms of the element placed side by side in a crystal. Option A describes the electronic radius, C is the nuclear radius, and D refers to bond length, not atomic radius.

mcqs.question: Covalent radius of an element is best described as:

options.A: Half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms bonded covalently
options.B: The distance from the nucleus to the outermost electron in a free atom
options.D: The distance between two non‑bonded atoms in a solid

mcqs.answer: Half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms bonded covalently
mcqs.explanation: When two identical atoms share a covalent bond, the internuclear distance is measured; half of this distance is defined as the covalent radius. Options B and C are unrelated, and D describes van der Waals radius, not covalent radius.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the van der Waals radius of an atom?

options.A: It is the distance from the nucleus to the outermost electron in an isolated atom
options.B: It is half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms that are bonded covalently
options.C: It is the distance between the nuclei of two non‑bonded atoms of the same element when they are in closest contact
options.D: It is the radius of the atomic nucleus

mcqs.answer: It is the distance between the nuclei of two non‑bonded atoms of the same element when they are in closest contact
mcqs.explanation: Van der Waals radius represents the size of an atom when it is not chemically bonded, measured as half the distance between two identical atoms that are merely touching each other in a solid. Option A describes electronic radius, B is covalent radius, and D is nuclear radius.

mcqs.question: Among the elements Li, Be, B, and C (all in the same period), which one has the smallest atomic radius?
mcqs.explanation: Across a period, atomic radius decreases from left to right because the increase in nuclear charge pulls the electron cloud closer, while the principal quantum level remains the same. Hence, carbon, being the farthest to the right among the listed elements, has the smallest radius. Options A‑C are larger for the same reason.

mcqs.question: Statement: "All elements in a group have the same atomic radius because they have the same number of valence electrons." Is this statement correct?
mcqs.explanation: Although elements in a group share the same valence electron configuration, each successive element adds an entire electron shell, increasing the distance between the nucleus and the outermost electrons. Therefore atomic radius increases down a group, making the statement false. Options C and D incorrectly limit the misconception to a subset of elements.

mcqs.question: Which ion has a larger ionic radius, K⁺ or Br⁻, and why?

options.A: K⁺ is larger because it loses an electron, reducing electron‑electron repulsion
options.B: Br⁻ is larger because gaining an electron increases electron‑electron repulsion in the same shell
options.C: Both have the same radius because they have the same number of electrons
options.D: K⁺ is larger because it has a higher nuclear charge

mcqs.answer: Br⁻ is larger because gaining an electron increases electron‑electron repulsion in the same shell
mcqs.explanation: K⁺ and Br⁻ are isoelectronic (both have 18 electrons). However, K⁺ has a higher effective nuclear charge (19 protons) than Br⁻ (35 protons) but the same electron count, leading to a stronger pull on the electrons and a smaller radius. Gaining an electron to form Br⁻ adds repulsion, expanding the electron cloud, so Br⁻ is larger. Option A reverses the effect, C ignores nuclear charge, and D misattributes size to nuclear charge alone.
